title: How Does Your Phone Hear 'Hey Google' When Locked?
hooks: Phone band hai, screen black hai... fir 'Hey Google' bolte hi ye jaag kaise jaata hai?
Kya Google aapki har baat chupke se 24 ghante sun raha hai?
Screen band hone par phone ko kaise pata chalta hai ki aapne usse pukara?
hook_why: Starts with an everyday relatable mystery on a locked phone that everyone experiences daily.
metaphor: A tiny sleeping guard chip that only wakes up when it hears one exact secret acoustic knock.

scenes.vo: Phone is off, screen is black. Then how does it wake up to 'Hey Google'?
scenes.prompt: Cinematic macro shot of a sleek matte black smartphone on dark surface, black locked screen, soft subtle glowing blue audio indicator ripples at bottom chin, photorealistic clean product lighting on pure black background, no text.
scenes.label: LOCKED PHONE

scenes.vo: Is Google secretly listening to your every word 24/7? Absolutely not!
If your phone uploaded everything to the internet, the battery would die in two hours.
scenes.label: BATTERY REALITY

scenes.vo: So what is the secret? There is a tiny acoustic DSP chip inside your phone.
scenes.prompt: Macro studio shot of a tiny isolated silicon DSP processor chip with micro-etched golden circuit pins, soft blue edge glow, pitch black studio background, no text, no labels.
scenes.label: DSP CHIP

scenes.vo: The main CPU sleeps deeply, but this tiny chip stands guard constantly.
scenes.label: POWER SAVING

scenes.vo: It records nothing. It just loops the last two seconds of audio.
scenes.title: AUDIO BUFFER
scenes.label: BUFFER LOOP

scenes.vo: Every new second deletes the old audio instantly! No internet, no storage used.
scenes.label: Storage
scenes.title: Auto Delete

scenes.vo: But the moment the sound frequency of 'Hey Google' matches exactly...
scenes.prompt: Abstract glowing golden acoustic soundwave spectrum sliding perfectly into a mechanical glowing waveform template, dark clean minimalist studio render, photorealistic, no text.
scenes.label: PATTERN MATCH

scenes.vo: This DSP instantly wakes up the main processor, and the screen lights up.
scenes.label: WAKE TRIGGER

scenes.vo: Does your phone unlock with a friend's voice too? Test it and tell me!

caption:
How does 'Hey Google' activate even when the screen is off and locked? Discover the hidden low-power DSP chip and 2-second buffer mechanism! Does your phone wake up to anyone else's voice?

Music: Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0

claims.claim: Modern smartphones use a low-power digital signal processor (DSP) to detect the wake-word locally without running the main application processor.
claims.basis: Documented in Qualcomm Snapdragon Hexagon DSP architecture and Android Open Source Project (AOSP) SoundTrigger HAL.

claims.claim: The wake-word detector listens in a short rolling circular buffer (typically 1 to 2 seconds) that continuously purges without saving audio to disk or uploading to servers.
claims.basis: Google Assistant privacy whitepaper on on-device hotword verification and local acoustic model processing.

claims.claim: Only after the hardware DSP verifies the local wake-word pattern does it send an interrupt to wake the main CPU and activate internet-connected speech recognition.
claims.basis: Google Pixel and Android SoundTrigger hardware interrupt documentation.
